test-types.title: Test Types
test-types.html:
IELTS is available in several formats depending on your purpose. Choose the version required by your university, employer, immigration authority, or professional body.

IELTS Academic

Designed for higher education and professional registration. Reading and Writing focus on academic texts, charts, arguments, and formal essay skills.

IELTS General Training

Usually used for migration, work, and training. Reading and Writing include more everyday workplace and social contexts.

IELTS UKVI

A secure version accepted for certain UK visa and immigration routes. The content is similar, but the administration follows UKVI requirements.

test-information.title: Test Information
test-information.html:
The IELTS exam evaluates four language skills: Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking. Listening, Reading, and Writing are normally completed on the same day. Speaking may be scheduled on the same day or nearby date.

SectionTimeFocusBest preparation habit
ListeningAbout 30 minutesUnderstanding recordings and answering in real timePractice prediction and spelling
Reading60 minutesFinding information and understanding meaningTime each passage strictly
Writing60 minutesTask 1 report/letter and Task 2 essayUse planning and feedback
Speaking11–14 minutesInterview, long turn, and discussionRecord and review answers

band-scores.title: Band Scores
band-scores.html:
IELTS results are reported on a 0–9 band scale. Each section receives a band score, and the overall band is calculated from the four components.

Band 5–6

Communication is possible, but errors, limited range, or incomplete task response can reduce clarity.

Band 6.5–7

Generally effective communication with better control, stronger organization, and fewer meaning-blocking errors.

Band 7.5–9

Strong flexibility, precise vocabulary, accurate grammar, and confident handling of complex ideas.

candidate.title: IELTS Candidate
candidate.html:
• Check the exact IELTS version required before booking.
  • Bring accepted identification on test day.
  • Practice under timed conditions, not only with untimed lessons.
  • Keep a mistake log for spelling, grammar, question types, and timing.
  • Use official-style answer sheets to reduce test-day surprises.

success-tips.title: Success Tips
success-tips.html:
Practice like the real exam

Use timers, answer sheets, no pausing, and quiet conditions. Reflection after each test matters more than simply doing more tests.

Get feedback for productive skills

Writing and Speaking scores improve faster when you identify patterns: weak development, grammar range, repetition, pronunciation, or cohesion problems.

Review errors weekly

Separate errors into vocabulary, grammar, timing, misunderstanding, and carelessness. Then build mini-lessons from those patterns.

Protect your confidence

Use a realistic roadmap. Avoid comparing your timeline to other candidates because starting levels and target scores differ.

prepare.title: How to Prepare
prepare.html:
1. Diagnose: Take a timed placement test and identify skill gaps.
  2. Learn: Study question types, band descriptors, and task expectations.
  3. Practice: Complete focused exercises before full tests.
  4. Review: Keep a mistake log and rewrite weak answers.
  5. Simulate: Take full mock exams weekly near your test date.
  6. Refine: Target your lowest skill with teacher or peer feedback.

gt-computer.title: GT IELTS & Computer IELTS
gt-computer.html:
General Training IELTS

Best for many migration and work purposes. Writing Task 1 is a letter, and reading texts are usually more everyday, workplace, or training focused.

Computer IELTS

Best for candidates comfortable typing and reading on screen. Results may be faster depending on provider, and editing written answers can feel easier.

FormatProsCons
Computer-basedEasy editing, typing, screen timer, often convenient slotsRequires typing speed and screen reading comfort
Paper-basedFamiliar handwriting and annotation experienceHarder editing and handwriting clarity matters

remarking.title: Remarking / EOR
remarking.html:
Enquiry on Results, also called EOR, is a remarking request. It may be useful when you strongly believe one or more component scores do not reflect your performance.

  • Check the deadline and fee with your test provider.
  • Writing and Speaking are more likely to change than Listening or Reading because they involve examiner judgment.
  • If the score changes, providers may refund the remarking fee depending on their rules.
  • Do not rely on remarking as a preparation strategy; use it only when there is a strong reason.

resources.title: Useful Links & Resources
resources.html:
Band descriptor checklist

Use this to evaluate Writing and Speaking performance against task response, coherence, vocabulary, grammar, fluency, and pronunciation.

Vocabulary tracker

Record topic vocabulary with sentence examples rather than isolated translations.

Mock test planner

Schedule full tests, review days, and targeted practice blocks so preparation stays balanced.

books.title: Recommended Books
books.html:
Official practice materials

Prioritize official-style practice tests for accurate format, difficulty, and answer key logic.

Skill-focused books

Use separate resources for IELTS Writing, academic vocabulary, grammar for accuracy, and reading strategies.

How to choose

Pick books with answer explanations, sample essays, model speaking responses, and progressive practice.

Study warning

Do not collect too many books. One good book completed carefully is better than five books skimmed quickly.

listening.title: Listening
listening.html:
Tips & Techniques

Preview questions, predict grammar type, listen for signposting, and watch for distractors when speakers correct themselves.

Free Lessons

Practice map labeling, multiple choice, form completion, and lecture note completion with short daily drills.

Example Material

Try a 10-question mini set, then check spelling, plural forms, word limit, and capitalization consistency.

reading.title: Reading
reading.html:
Tips & Techniques

Read the question first, locate keywords and paraphrases, then read around the answer sentence carefully.

Free Lessons

Focus on True/False/Not Given, matching headings, sentence completion, and matching information.

Example Material

Use one passage for three goals: timing, question type review, and vocabulary extraction.

writing.title: Writing
writing.html:
Writing Tips & Techniques

Analyze the task, plan paragraph roles, use clear topic sentences, and leave time to check grammar and word forms.

Task 1 Guidance

Identify overview trends, compare key data, avoid listing every number, and use precise language for increase, decrease, stability, and contrast.

Task 2 Guidance

Answer every part of the question, develop ideas with explanation and examples, and maintain a clear position throughout the essay.

Sample Answers

Study model answers by asking: What is the paragraph purpose? How is the idea extended? What grammar and vocabulary patterns are reusable?

Common Mistakes

Memorized introductions, weak examples, overgeneralization, sentence fragments, informal tone, and poor time management reduce scores.

Band Score Improvement

Improve one criterion at a time: task response, coherence and cohesion, lexical resource, or grammatical range and accuracy.

speaking.title: Speaking
speaking.html:
Tips & Techniques

Answer directly, extend with reasons and examples, use natural linking, and avoid memorized speeches.

Free Lessons

Practice Part 1 personal questions, Part 2 cue cards, and Part 3 abstract discussion questions.

Example Material

Record yourself twice: first for fluency, second for grammar correction and vocabulary upgrade.
